inputs.revenue_basis: base_revenue is CORE revenue ex-construction: FY2025 reported 20,289.2 less construction revenue 8,155.6 (quarterly split 1,797.3/1,725.8/342.6/4,289.9, AR p.11) = 12,133.6 (company states ~RMB12.134bn). Construction revenue is a zero-margin IFRIC-12/PRC concession pass-through equal to construction services expense 8,155.6; its cash cost sits in capex. Toll revenue 9,555 (+0.29%). Core EBITDA FY2025 = core revenue - (operating costs 14,188.0 - construction 8,155.6) - taxes & surcharges 88.7 - selling 5.7 - G&A 282.1 + D&A 2,609.4 + other income ex the 52m one-off Xiyi grant 14.9 = ~8,349 (68.8%); FY2024 same basis ~8,237 on 12,332 (66.8%).
inputs.wacc_rationale: RMB-built: 10y CGB ~1.9%; cost of equity ~8.0% (beta ~0.8 on a 7.6% China ERP incl. country premium, appropriate for an offshore H-share holder); pre-tax cost of debt 2.26% FY2025 (normalised 2.5%) -> 1.9% after 25% tax; ~60/40 E/D at market -> ~5.6%; rounded UP to 6.0% for refinancing/rate-reversal risk on a growing debt load. Same WACC in every scenario (risk charged once, in the flows). Gordon at 6%/2% would be ~25x terminal FCF, so the cap binds in every scenario (base 18x = ~7.7% equivalent yield at 2% growth). Finite concession life is charged ONCE: in the base/bull flows as renewal capex, in the bear as a 12x cap with no renewal capex.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): lease liabilities (29.8m) left in total_debt; immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (including 100% of Xitai/Danjin capex and future tolls); NCI deducted ONCE in the bridge at 31-Mar-2026 book value 13,864.7. NCI earns only ~228m/yr today because most of it is partner equity contributed to construction-stage subsidiaries (Xitai 47.5% owned, Danjin) -- book is the right measure of a claim that is still mostly cash-at-cost. Future partner contributions offset their share of the remaining capex (value-neutral if the projects earn ~WACC). FY0 tie: modelled EBIT ~5,740 x 0.75 + associates 790 + BoJ dividend 168 - after-tax interest ~620 = ~4,600-4,900 vs reported total NPAT 4,821 / attributable 4,594.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with the non-US adaptations (currency, NCI, non-operating assets, SBC-zero), routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md: a toll-concession operator is an operating company whose value is a cash-flow stream; it is not a bank/REIT/holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). Concession-life handling: concessions are finite (toll road operating rights amortised over 25-35-year franchise periods by traffic) and the core Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway (~RMB15.1m/day, ~57% of toll revenue) is understood from market sources to reach the end of its toll period around 2032 -- the expiry date is NOT disclosed in the extracted filings and is unverified. Base assumes the company's established route of a reconstruction-and-expansion programme that extends the toll period (as on Xiyi, Guangjing, Ningyang), carried as a 2031-2034 capex wave at 32-35% of revenue and terminal capex 30% (> D&A 24%, i.e. reinvestment sufficient to keep a finite-life portfolio perpetual at 2% growth). Bear lets the Shanghai-Nanjing concession lapse to a reduced maintenance toll. FCF base: reported FCF is negative (FY2025 -865) because 2024-2028 is a capex supercycle (Xitai RMB24.2bn 31% complete, Danjin RMB14.6bn 23%, Guangjing North 2.9bn 26%, Xiyi South 75%, Ningyang North opened 1-Jan-2026); no trough or peak year is extrapolated -- the component build carries the committed project capex explicitly (FY2026 plan RMB11.75bn incl. a 500m Zijin Trust capital increase that is an investment, not capex, and ~85% plan-to-cash conversion as in FY2025: plan 8,965 vs cash 7,626) and the tolls those roads earn from 2029. PRC OCF excludes interest paid and investment returns received, so it is an unlevered, ex-investment-income operating flow consistent with the bridge. Buybacks: none; the flat count needs no funding because there is no SBC. Pending Suxichang South acquisition (RMB7.34bn cash, related party, Aug-2026) is not in the flows; it is treated as near-NPV-zero with a related-party valuation haircut in the bridge. Balance sheet is the latest filing available locally (Q1-2026, 31-Mar-2026); the H1-2026 interim (Aug-2026) is not extracted -- replace the anchors when it is. Q1 report mislabels long-term equity investments as 'Other debt investment' (13,748.6; ties to 13,522.5 at Dec-25). Cap sensitivity: an earlier pass at the house 15x/17x/12x caps gave base HK$8.03, bull HK$12.90, weighted HK$7.49; that stacked a 15x finite-life haircut on top of the renewal capex already in the flows, so the base was moved to 18x and the bull to 20x.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.0% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 20.4% and EPS 5yr 13.3%. All three are distorted: revenue by the construction pass-through (8.2bn of 20.3bn in FY2025) and the FY2020 COVID toll-free base; EPS by the same 2020 base; equity by RMB4.9bn of OCI fair-value gains on the Bank of Jiangsu stake. Toll revenue was flat FY2023-25 (+0.2%/yr) during widening works. The DCF does not use selected_growth_rate; driver paths are built bottom-up.

base.growth_rates_note: Core revenue ex-construction. FY2026: H1 core +2.16%, tolls +5.76% (Ningyang North and Xiyi South open) offset by fuel, energy and property. FY2029 +10%: Xitai (RMB24.2bn) and Danjin (RMB14.6bn) open end-2028 at a ~3.5% first-year revenue yield on cost (~RMB1.3bn), ramping through 2031.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY2025 68.8%, FY2024 66.8% (core basis). Mix shifts to tolls (~80%+ margin) as widening disruption ends and new roads open; fuel resale shrinks.
base.capex_note: ~RMB9.8bn FY2026 (plan 11.75bn less 0.5bn Zijin Trust at ~85% cash conversion), ~10.5bn FY2027, ~9.0bn FY2028, ~3.9bn FY2029 settlements -- ~33bn over 2026-29 against ~34bn remaining on the committed pipeline. 2031-34 Shanghai-Nanjing reconstruction/expansion wave that buys the toll-period extension; terminal 30% vs D&A 24%.
base.terminal_note: Cap 18x terminal FCF (~7.6x terminal EV/EBITDA, below today's ~8.3x core EV/EBITDA). Concession renewal is already charged in the flows (2031-34 expansion wave, terminal capex 30% vs D&A 24%), so the cap is not used as a second finite-life haircut; at 15x the base falls to ~HK$8.0 (sensitivity recorded in notes).

bull.capex_note: Same RMB project spend as base; lower % because revenue is higher.

bear.growth_rates_note: Weak Jiangsu freight, more mandated discounts, slow Xitai/Danjin ramp; Shanghai-Nanjing toll period ends ~mid-2032 without an extension and reverts to a reduced maintenance toll (2032-33 core revenue down ~25% in total).
bear.capex_note: Committed pipeline spent in full (same RMB as base, higher % on lower revenue); no Shanghai-Nanjing expansion wave because the concession is not extended.
bear.terminal_note: Cap 12x: no renewal capex in the bear flows, so the finite-life haircut sits in the multiple instead.

scenario_narratives.base: Tolls grow 3-4%/yr as the Xiyi and Ningyang works finish and Jiangsu traffic keeps growing. Xitai and Danjin open at end-2028 after ~RMB33bn more capex and ramp from a low ~3.5% revenue yield on cost. Core margin drifts from 69% to 72% as tolls take a bigger share than fuel resale. The Shanghai-Nanjing toll period is renewed the way Jiangsu has renewed others: a 2031-34 reconstruction-and-expansion programme that costs a third of revenue for four years. Owner FCF is negative until 2029, so most of the value sits in the terminal and in the non-operating book (Bank of Jiangsu, associates). That book is worth ~RMB5.3/share after deferred tax, or ~RMB2.5 once NCI is deducted at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Yangtze River Delta freight and new-energy vehicle traffic push tolls up 4%+. The new roads ramp faster (+12% in 2029). Service-area 'Transportation+' and YS Energy lift margins to 73%. The Shanghai-Nanjing extension and the Suxichang South profit guarantee land cleanly. The toll-highway regulation revision formalises concession extension for expansion projects, which supports a 17x terminal.
scenario_narratives.bear: Toll policy bites: more mandated truck/holiday discounts and differentiated pricing, and the long-pending Toll Highway Regulation revision tightens concession terms. Jiangsu freight softens and the new roads ramp slowly. The Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway, about 57% of tolls, reaches the end of its toll period around 2032 with no extension and falls to a maintenance toll. Meanwhile the whole committed pipeline is still spent with debt, and the related-party Suxichang South deal is overpaid. Terminal 12x at 1% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default) for the single-regulator dependency: toll rates, discounts and, above all, the Shanghai-Nanjing concession renewal sit with provincial/national authorities, and the regulation revision has been pending since 2013. Base 50%, as the established extension-by-expansion route has worked on several of the company's own roads. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs faster traffic, a smooth new-road ramp and a favourable regulation all at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated toll-concession operator valued on core (ex-construction) owner FCF with the committed capex supercycle explicit, plus a separately itemised non-operating book. Finite concession life is handled in the flows (renewal capex) and in a 15x terminal cap rather than in the discount rate. The H-share's ~5% dividend yield reflects distributions funded partly by borrowing during the capex cycle, not free cash flow.
key_risks_to_valuation: Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway toll-period expiry (~2032, unverified from filings) and the terms of any extension
Revision of the Regulations for the Administration of Toll Highways
